'''Malcolm Iseiah Thomas''' (born November 8, 1988) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played  for the [[Sagesse SC (basketball)|Sagesse Club]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]] (LBL). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball|San Diego State Aztecs]], where he twice earned second-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]] (MWC) honors.

==Early life==
Thomas was born in [[Columbia, Missouri]], to his father, also named [[Malcolm Thomas (basketball, born 1963)|Malcolm Thomas]], and Lori Dawson.<ref name=sdsu_bio>{{cite web|title=Player Bio: Malcolm Thomas |publisher=San Diego State University |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/sdsu/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/ThomasUpdatedPlayerBio.pdf |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304112422/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/sdsu/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/ThomasUpdatedPlayerBio.pdf |archivedate=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> His father was an honorable mention [[All-American]] basketball player at [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]] and drafted in the sixth round of the [[1985 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref name=ziegler_05082011>{{cite news |last=Ziegler |first=Mark |title=Aztecs' Thomas draws inspiration from daughter |date=March 8, 2011 |newspaper=San Diego Union-Tribune |url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/mar/08/aztecs-thomas-draws-inspiration-daughter/?print&page=all |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313202622/http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/mar/08/aztecs-thomas-draws-inspiration-daughter/?print&page=all |archivedate=March 13, 2016 |url-status=dead |access-date=December 14, 2011 }}</ref>

The younger Thomas was raised by his mother and aunts, while his father was not always around.<ref name=ziegler_05082011/> Thomas played at [[Crawford High School (California)|Crawford High School]] in [[San Diego, California]], helping Crawford to a [[California Interscholastic Federation]] (CIF) section title in his senior year.<ref name="sdsu_bio"/>

==College career==
[[File:Malcolm Thomas dunking cropped.jpg|left|thumb|180px|Thomas dunking]]
Thomas averaged 12.5 points and 8.8 rebounds as freshman at [[Pepperdine Waves men's basketball|Pepperdine University]].  He transferred to [[San Diego City College]] and averaged 21.1 points, 12.9 rebounds and 3.9 blocks and was named [[California Community College Athletic Association]] (CCCAA) co-[[Most Valuable Player]] (MVP) and the [[Pacific Coast Conference]] Player of the Year.<ref name=sdsu_bio/> He [[NBA early entry|declared early]] for the [[2009 NBA draft]], but withdrew after one NBA workout.<ref name=ziegler_06202011>{{cite news |last=Zielgler |first=Mark |title=SDSU's Thomas looks like a draft lock |date=June 20, 2011 |newspaper=The San Diego Union-Tribune |url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/jun/20/sdsus-thomas-looks-draft-lock/?print&page=all |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310124231/http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/jun/20/sdsus-thomas-looks-draft-lock/?print&page=all |archivedate=March 10, 2016 |url-status=dead |access-date=December 19, 2011 }}</ref>

He went on to play two seasons at SDSU and twice earned All-MWC second team honors. In his senior year, he was named 2011 All-MWC defensive team after finishing second in the conference in [[rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] and [[blocked shot]]s.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Mountain West Conference Announces 2010–11 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards |publisher=[[Mountain West Conference]] |url=http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030711aaf.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111226055048/http://www.themwc.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030711aaf.html |archivedate=December 26, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Draft's Potential Celtics: San Diego State F Malcolm Thomas |work=[[WEEI-FM|WEEI.com]] |url=http://greenstreet.weei.com/sports/boston/basketball/celtics/2011/06/21/nba-drafts-potential-celtics-san-diego-state-f-malcolm-thomas/ |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110829225645/http://greenstreet.weei.com/sports/boston/basketball/celtics/2011/06/21/nba-drafts-potential-celtics-san-diego-state-f-malcolm-thomas/ |archivedate=August 29, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The team advanced to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Sweet 16]] that season. He ended his two-year career with the Aztecs as the school's second leading all-time shot blocker and ranked eighth all-time in both rebound average and [[field goal percentage]].<ref>{{cite news|title=LAKERS ASSIGN ANDREW GOUDELOCK AND MALCOLM THOMAS TO LOS ANGELES D-FENDERS |date=December 17, 2011 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/111217goudelock_thomas.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120110185701/http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/111217goudelock_thomas.html |archivedate=January 10, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Professional career==

===2011–12===
Thomas went [[undrafted sportsperson|undrafted]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. During the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]] that summer, he signed a $350,000 contract to play a season for [[Mobis Phoebus]] in the [[Korean Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Amick |first=Sam |title=NBA stars looking abroad in earnest |work=SI.com |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/sam_amick/07/24/amick.notebook/index.html |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120728121720/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/sam_amick/07/24/amick.notebook/index.html |archivedate=July 28, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Most overseas rookies made about $100,000–$150,000.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ziegler |first=Mark |title=SDSU's Thomas signs with Korean pro team |date=July 6, 2011 |newspaper=The San Diego Union-Tribune |url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/jul/06/sdsus-thomas-signs-korean-pro-team/ |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110915070946/http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/jul/06/sdsus-thomas-signs-korean-pro-team/ |archivedate=September 15, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The team released him in November 2011, despite his averaging 21 points, 11 rebounds, three blocks, and three assists. They wanted a more veteran player, but agreed to pay the remainder of Thomas' salary.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ziegler |first=Mark |title=SDSU's Thomas returns from Korea |date=November 28, 2011 |newspaper=The San Diego Union-Tribune |url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/nov/28/sdsus-thomas-returns-korea/?print&page=all |archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120909212042/http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2011/nov/28/sdsus-thomas-returns-korea/?print&page=all |archivedate=September 9, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Thomas was signed by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on December 13, 2011.<ref>{{cite news|last=Medina |first=Mark |title=Lakers sign Gerald Green, Malcolm Thomas |date=December 13, 2011 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/12/lakers-sign-gerald-green-malcolm-thomas.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107222647/http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/12/lakers-sign-gerald-green-malcolm-thomas.html |archivedate=January 7, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 17, he was [[Assignment (NBA D-League)|assigned]] to the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] by the Lakers, and was recalled the next day.<ref name="LATIMESBLOG">{{cite news|url=http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/12/lakers-send-andrew-goudelock-marcus-thomas-to-d-fenders.html|title=Lakers send Andrew Goudelock, Marcus Thomas to D-Fenders|date=December 17, 2011|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|accessdate=December 19, 2011}}</ref><ref name=201112_transactions>{{cite web|title=2011–12 Transactions |work=NBA.com |publisher=NBA Media Ventures |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/transactions_201112.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131031004037/http://www.nba.com/dleague/transactions_201112.html |archivedate=October 31, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was [[waivers (NBA)|waived]] by the Lakers before the start of the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Media |date=December 22, 2011 |first=Mark |title=Lakers cut roster to 15 players |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |url=http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/12/lakers-cut-roster-to-15-players.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120108101942/http://lakersblog.latimes.com/lakersblog/2011/12/lakers-cut-roster-to-15-players.html |archivedate=January 8, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was signed by the D-Fenders on December 28.<ref>{{cite press release|title=D-FENDERS ACQUIRE GERALD GREEN AND MALCOLM THOMAS |date=December 28, 2011 |publisher=Los Angeles D-Fenders |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/111228_acquire_green_thomas.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203062453/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/111228_acquire_green_thomas.html |archivedate=February 3, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On January 11, 2012, Thomas was then signed by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], where he was reunited with former Aztec teammate [[Kawhi Leonard]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Spurs waive Diogu, reunite rookie Leonard with ex-San Diego State teammate Thomas |date=January 11, 2012 |newspaper=The Washington Post |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/spurs-waive-diogu-reunite-rookie-leonard-with-ex-san-diego-state-teammate-thomas/2012/01/11/gIQA3F6SrP_story.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120116160847/http://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/spurs-waive-diogu-reunite-rookie-leonard-with-ex-san-diego-state-teammate-thomas/2012/01/11/gIQA3F6SrP_story.html |archivedate=January 16, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played in his first NBA game on January 13 against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], getting one rebound in two minutes of [[garbage time]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Price |first=Tim |title=Notebook: Spurs 99, Blazers 83 |date=January 14, 2012 |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120113/PORSAS/gameinfo.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120210090604/http://www.nba.com/games/20120113/PORSAS/gameinfo.html |archivedate=February 10, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Thomas was assigned to the [[Austin Toros]] on January 30.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120130_malcolm_thomas_assigned_to_austin_toros |title=Spurs Assign Malcolm Thomas to Austin Toros |publisher=Nba.com |date=January 30, 2012 |accessdate=March 9, 2013}}</ref> On February 7, the Spurs waived Thomas.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Spurs Place Malcolm Thomas on Waivers| date= February 7, 2012|publisher=San Antonio Spurs| url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120207_spurs_waive_malcolm_thomas}}</ref> He joined the D-Fenders again on February 9.<ref name=201112_transactions/>

Later that season, he signed with the [[Houston Rockets]], who assigned him to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/riograndevalley/RocketsAssignThomas033012.html |title=Rockets Assign Malcolm Thomas to Vipers |publisher=Nba.com |date=March 30, 2012 |accessdate=March 9, 2013}}</ref> He then rejoined the D-Fenders, with whom he played in the D-League finals.<ref>{{cite news|title=Austin beats LA, evens D-League finals |date=April 28, 2012 |newspaper=Erie Times-News |url=http://www.goerie.com/article/20120428/BASKETBALL05/304289921/Austin-beats-LA-evens-D-League-finals |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120519202222/http://goerie.com/article/20120428/BASKETBALL05/304289921/Austin-beats-LA-evens-D-League-finals |archivedate=May 19, 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2012–13===
On October 3, 2012, Thomas signed a one-year contract with [[EuroLeague]] club [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of Israel.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.maccabi.co.il/News.asp?id=3614&language=english |title=Malcolm Thomas Signs with Maccabi Electra Tel Aviv |date=October 3, 2012 |publisher=Maccabi Tel-Aviv Basketball Club |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201202412/http://www.maccabi.co.il/News.asp?id=3614&language=english |archivedate=February 1, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Steinberg |first=Jessica |title=Maccabi Tel Aviv signs US recruit |date=October 3, 2012 |publisher=The Times of Israel |url=https://www.timesofisrael.com/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-u-s-recruit/ |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006025144/https://www.timesofisrael.com/maccabi-tel-aviv-signs-u-s-recruit/ |archivedate=October 6, 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> In competition in Israel, he averaged 7.4 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 1.3 blocks, and in EuroLeague competition he had a [[double-double]] of 14 points and 11 rebounds in 26 minutes in a 70–68 victory over Italian [[Montepaschi Siena]] in mid-October.<ref name="sportando1">{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/israel/50422/maccabi-and-malcolm-thomas-are-no-more.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130205054727/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/israel/50422/maccabi-and-malcolm-thomas-are-no-more.html |archivedate=February 5, 2013|title=Maccabi and Malcolm Thomas are no more |publisher=Sportando.net |date=February 2, 2013 |accessdate=July 30, 2015}}</ref>  However, after Tel Aviv signed 6-foot-11 Croatian [[Darko Planinić]], his minutes decreased.<ref name="sportando1"/>  Thomas was waived by Maccabi Tel Aviv in February 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/basketball.aspx?NewsID=306142 |title=Maccabi Electra Tel-Aviv and Malcolm Thomas part ways |publisher=Eurobasket.com |date= |accessdate=March 9, 2013}}</ref>

On March 5, he rejoined the Los Angeles D-Fenders.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/130305_malcolmthomas.html |title=Malcolm Thomas returns to the D-Fenders |publisher=NBA.com |date=March 5, 2013 |accessdate=March 8, 2013}}</ref> On March 8, Thomas was called up from the D-League and signed a 10-day contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Malcom Thomas To 10-Day Contract |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-malcom-thomas-10-day-contract |work=NBA.com |date=March 8, 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160413163738/http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-malcom-thomas-10-day-contract |archivedate=April 13, 2016 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was assigned to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the NBA D-League on March 12, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Golden State Warriors Assign Kent Bazemore and Malcolm Thomas to NBA D-League Affiliate Santa Cruz Warriors|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/warriors_assign_bazemore_thomas_2013_03_12.html|work=NBA.com|date=March 12, 2013|accessdate=March 12, 2013}}</ref> He was recalled a day later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html |title=2012–13 Transactions |work=NBA.com |date=March 13, 2013 |accessdate=March 13, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111101144313/http://www.nba.com/dleague/dleague/transactions.html |archivedate=November 1, 2011 }}</ref>

On March 19, 2013, Thomas signed a 10-day contract with the Chicago Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-forward-malcolm-thomas-10-day-contract.html |title=Bulls sign forward Malcolm Thomas to 10-day contract |publisher=Nba.com |date=March 19, 2013 |accessdate=November 9, 2013}}</ref> He signed a second 10-day contract on March 29,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-thomas-second-10-day-contract.html |title=Bulls sign Thomas to second 10-day contract |publisher=Nba.com |date= |accessdate=November 9, 2013}}</ref> and signed for the remainder of the season on April 8.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-thomas-remainder-season.html |title=Bulls sign Thomas for remainder of the season |publisher=Nba.com |date=April 8, 2013 |accessdate=November 9, 2013}}</ref> On July 23, he was waived by the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-forward-malcolm-thomas.html |title=Bulls waive forward Malcolm Thomas |publisher=Nba.com |date=July 23, 2013 |accessdate=November 9, 2013}}</ref>

===2013–14===
In November 2013, Thomas was reacquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/1314_training_camp_roster.html |title=2013–14 Training Camp Roster |work=NBA.com |date=November 4, 2013 |accessdate=November 9, 2013 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610060051/http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/1314_training_camp_roster.html |archivedate=June 10, 2016 }}</ref>

On December 3, 2013, Thomas signed with the San Antonio Spurs<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/131203_malcolm_thomas Spurs Sign Malcolm Thomas]</ref> and was assigned multiple time to the Austin Toros.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html 2013–14 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703151241/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2013_14.html |date=July 3, 2014 }}</ref> On January 23, 2014, he was waived by the Spurs.<ref>{{cite news|title=Spurs waive Malcolm Thomas|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/140123_spurs_waive_thomas|accessdate=January 23, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2014}}</ref> Two days later, he was claimed off waivers by the Utah Jazz.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jazz Claims Malcolm Thomas Off Waivers|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-claims-malcolm-thomas-waivers|accessdate=January 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2014}}</ref>

On February 3, 2014, Thomas was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html Eighth Annual NBA D-League All-Star Game Features 16 Players With NBA Experience] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140207181043/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/nba_dleague_all_star_2014_02_03.html |date=February 7, 2014 }}</ref>

===2014–15===
On July 22, 2014, Thomas was traded by Utah, along with [[John Lucas III]] and [[Erik Murphy]], to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in exchange for [[Carrick Felix]], a 2015 second round draft pick, and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/cavaliers-trade-140722|title=Cavaliers Acquire John Lucas III, Malcolm Thomas and Erik Murphy from Utah|date=July 22, 2014|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|accessdate=July 22, 2014}}</ref> On September 25, he was traded, along with John Lucas III, Erik Murphy, [[Dwight Powell]], and the Cavaliers' 2016 and 2017 second-round picks, to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Keith Bogans]] and two future second-round picks.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-announce-roster-moves Boston Celtics Announce Roster Moves]</ref> Four days later, he was waived by the Celtics.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-evan-turner Celtics Sign Evan Turner]</ref>

On October 27, 2014, Thomas signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141027-thomas-signed Sixers Sign Free Agent Malcolm Thomas]</ref> On November 10, he was waived by the 76ers after appearing in five games.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sixers Call Up Drew Gordon From Delaware 87ers|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141110-gordon-called-up|accessdate=November 10, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=November 10, 2014}}</ref> He had been playing with fluid and loose cartilage in his left knee.<ref>{{cite news|last=Pompey |first=Keith |title=Sixers sign Gordon, release Thomas |date=November 10, 2014 |newspaper=The Philadelphia Inquirer |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/deep-sixer/Sixers-sign-Gordon-release-Thomas.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110214502/http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/deep-sixer/Sixers-sign-Gordon-release-Thomas.html |archivedate=November 10, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> On December 23, 2014, he re-signed with the 76ers.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/141223-thomas-signed Sixers Sign Free Agent Malcolm Thomas]</ref> On February 22, 2015, he was waived again by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sixers Sign Ishmael Smith|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150222-smith-signed|accessdate=February 22, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=February 22, 2015}}</ref>

In April 2015, Thomas signed with the [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of Puerto Rico.<ref>{{cite news|title=Malcolm Thomas agreed terms with Quebradillas|url=http://www.latinbasket.com/Puerto-Rico/news/400360/Malcolm-Thomas-agreed-terms-with-Quebradillas|accessdate=April 2, 2015|work=Eurobasket.com|date=April 2, 2015}}</ref>

===2015–16===
On October 31, 2015, Thomas was acquired by the Los Angeles D-Fenders, returning to the franchise for a fourth stint.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=5065520|title=D-Fenders Finalize 2015 Training Camp Roster|date=October 31, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com|accessdate=November 1, 2015}}</ref> On January 29, 2016, he left the D-Fenders to sign with the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association|Philippines]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://onemeralcosports.com/bolts/maclolm-thomas-named-commissioners-cup-import/|title=Malcolm Thomas Named Commissioner's Cup Import|date=January 29, 2016|work=OneMeralcoSports.com|accessdate=January 29, 2016}}</ref> However, on February 6, 2016, he was released by the Bolts after suffering an injury before the start of the [[2016 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Karlo|last=Sacamos|title=Arinze Onuaku replaces injured Malcolm Thomas in last-minute import change for Bolts|url=http://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/arinze-onuaku-replaces-injured-malcolm-thomas-in-last-minute-import-change-for-meralco|work=Spin.ph|date=February 6, 2016|accessdate=February 6, 2016}}</ref>

===2016–17===
On July 30, 2016, Thomas signed with [[Jilin Northeast Tigers]] of China for the [[2016–17 CBA season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Malcolm Thomas (ex Meralco Bolts) agreed terms with Jilin Tigers for 1-year $0.7M|url=http://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/456415/Malcolm-Thomas-(ex-Meralco-Bolts)-agreed-terms-with-Jilin-Tigers-for-1-year-$0.7M|work=Asia-Basket.com|date=July 30, 2016|accessdate=February 6, 2016}}</ref>

===2017–19===
On July 20, 2017, Thomas signed a two-year deal with Russian club [[BC Khimki|Khimki]] of the [[VTB United League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BC Khimki lands Malcolm Thomas|url=http://en.bckhimki.ru/news/clubnews/2017/july/1224/|work=en.bckhimki.ru|date=July 20, 2017|accessdate=July 20, 2017}}</ref>

===2019–20===
On December 23, 2019, Thomas was reported to have signed with [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe Beko]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Malcolm Thomas Fenerbahçe Beko'da|language=TR|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2019/12-son/malcolm-thomas-fenerbahce-beko-da|date=December 23, 2019|website=fenerbahce.org|accessdate=December 23, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Basketball: Malcolm Thomas joins Fenerbahce Beko Turkish club signs deal with US-born player through end of this season|url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/basketball-malcolm-thomas-joins-fenerbahce-beko/1681691|date=December 23, 2019|website=aa.com.tr|accessdate=December 23, 2019}}</ref> He averaged 2.9 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game in 12 games.<ref name=bayern/>

===2020–21===
On July 28, 2020, he signed a one-year deal with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL) with the option for another season.<ref name=bayern>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fc-bayern-announces-malcolm-thomas/|title=FC Bayern announces Malcolm Thomas|last=|first=|date=July 28, 2020|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 28, 2020}}</ref> On December 3, 2020, Thomas and [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] parted ways.

===2021–22===
On November 17, 2021, he has signed 1,5 month contract with [[Petkim Spor]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL) with an option to extend until end of season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketservisi.com/2021/11/17/resmi-petkim-fenerbahcenin-eski-uzunu-ile-anlasti-analiz/|title=RESMİ: Petkim, Fenerbahçe’nin Eski Uzunu ile Anlaştı|last=|first=|date=November 17, 2021|website=basketservisi|publisher=|language=tr|access-date=November 17, 2021}}</ref>

===2022–23===
On August 19, 2022, he has signed with [[BC Samara]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bcsamara.com/news/?id=4733|title=Малкольм Томас — новичок "Самары"!|last=|first=|date=August 19, 2022|website=bcsamara.com|publisher=|language=ru|access-date=August 22, 2022}}</ref>

===2023–24===
On December 7, 2023, he signed with [[Büyükçekmece Basketbol|ONVO Büyükçekmece]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketfaul.com.tr/turkiye/bsl/eski-fenerbahceli-buyukcekmecede/|title=Eski Fenerbahçeli Büyükçekmece’de|last=|first=|date=December 7, 2023|website=|publisher=basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=December 7, 2023}}</ref>

===2024–25===
On January 12, 2025, Thomas signed with the [[Sagesse SC (basketball)|Sagesse SC]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]] (LBL).<ref>{{cite web |title=Sagesse inks Malcolm Thomas, ex Buyukcekmece |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/911643/Sagesse-inks-Malcolm-Thomas-ex-Buyukcekmece |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=January 12, 2025}}</ref>

=== The Basketball Tournament (TBT) (2017–present) ===
In the summer of 2017, Thomas played in [[The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for team A Few Good Men (Gonzaga Alumni). He competed for the $2 million prize, and for team A Few Good Men, he averaged 12.3 points per game and 7.5 rebounds per game. Thomas helped take team A Few Good Men to the Super 16 round, where they then lost to Team Challenge ALS 77–60.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thetournament.com/bracket|title=Bracket {{!}} The Basketball Tournament|website=www.thetournament.com|language=en|access-date=February 27, 2018}}</ref>
